title: tendcf — shared Site Model definitions
description: Definitions shared by every Site Model file. The three D16 fields (provides/requires, interlocks, comprehensive/opt_out_reason) live here because they are cross-cutting. Schemas live in tendcf (D21); nix2cf is the compiler. Current-design facts follow docs/paper/tendcf-architecture-guide.md.

contract_version.description: Bumped only when an EXISTING field is renamed, retyped, or removed. Adding a new optional field never needs a bump.

identifier.description: Lowercase kebab identifier used for domains, bundles, roles, and service names.

host_name.description: A host as named in the Site Model inventory/.

release_stamp.description: Identifier of the signed release that produced this row. Every reporting row carries it (guide §6; D19). Not a sibling-repo lockstep tag.

token.description: A name a type supplies or needs, stated locally (D16(b)). `kind:name`. A naming catalogue, not a permission: holding a token grants nothing. The kind set is closed so a typo is a schema error rather than a silently-unmatched edge — map §0 rule 6, prefer machine-checkable to conventional. Extending the set is additive.

provides.description: What this entry supplies. Local knowledge only: answerable from inside this one file (D16(b), R13).

requires.description: What this entry needs. nix2cf infers ordering edges by matching these against other entries' `provides`. Every inferred edge carries the rule that produced it (D16(b), edge attribution is mandatory).

depends_on.description: Authored ordering edges. Remains available and AUTHORITATIVE (D16(b)) — where an authored and an inferred edge exist for the same pair, the authored one wins and the coincidence is reported, never silently deduplicated. Prefer provides/requires: depends_on is global knowledge, which is what R13 rejects as the primary mechanism.

source_location.description: Where a declaration was written. Required in conflict errors (D16(a)) and on authored edges (D16(b)); nix2cf fills it in, authors do not write it.

interlock_argv.description: An interlock pre_action argv, held to an alphabet instead of being escaped. The bundle joins the argv with single spaces and hands the string to cf-agent's commands promise with useshell => noshell, which splits it again on whitespace and treats a leading " ' or ` as a quote (libpromises/exec_tools.c ArgSplitCommand); no shell runs, so `;`, `|`, `&&`, redirection and `$(` are inert there. The alphabet keeps that join/split lossless and keeps a shell-shaped argv out of the file even if a shell were ever reintroduced: ASCII letters, digits and `. _ + @ : = , / -`, one or more characters, no space, quote, backslash, `$`, `%`, glob or control character. command[0] additionally starts with `/`: the executable is an absolute path, never a PATH lookup. `not` forbids a newline anywhere because a `$`-anchored pattern in some regex engines (Python's) also matches before a trailing newline.

interlock.description: A stated precondition (D16(c), Bcfg2 Actions semantics). Compiles to a CFEngine guard class plus a bundle-scoped refusal: if the pre-action fails, EVERY entry in the enclosing bundle is blocked from modification and the failure is reported. Blast radius and reporting are consts, not author choices — that is what structurally closes 'VPN must be authenticated before lockdown may be enforced' rather than leaving it as a safe default plus a comment.

description.description: Plain language, for the human who has to resolve a block.

defines_class.description: CFEngine class defined when the pre-action succeeds; guarded promises key off it.

blocks.description: Fixed by decision: the enclosing bundle is simultaneously the grouping unit and the re-verify scope.

report.description: Fixed by decision: a blocked bundle is always reported centrally. Not an author choice.

domain_coverage.description: D16(d): a domain is COMPREHENSIVE unless it declares otherwise. Anything present on the device and absent from a comprehensive domain's description is reported as an extra entry — the only mechanism in the design that detects multi-writer skew at all. Opting out requires a reason from a closed set: a bare boolean would let an agent widen the unmanaged surface silently.

oneOf.description: Real device state nobody has described yet. Backlog, and COUNTABLE — this count is the build order's progress metric (guide §18 / map §13, Step 0). Normal day-one state for everything.
State that is genuinely not ours to describe (user data, another tool's territory, device-generated caches). Permanent, and should be rare.

then.$comment: Opting out without a reason is the R13 failure mode this field exists to prevent.
A reason on a comprehensive domain is a contradiction — usually a half-finished migration. Caught here rather than left to review.

outcome_enforce.description: ncf/Rudder's enforce-mode outcome vocabulary, kept verbatim (D17 — reuse the vocabulary, change only the sink).

outcome_audit.description: ncf/Rudder's audit-mode outcome vocabulary, kept verbatim.

env_map.description: Environment for a service. Values are secretspec key NAMES, never secret values. The generic layer holds nobody's facts and no secrets.

additionalProperties.description: A secretspec key name, resolved at run time by secretspec.
